blogPosts.title: How Much Does an Office Fitout Cost in Melbourne? (2026 Guide)
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about office fitout costs in Melbourne? We break down average prices per square metre in Southbank, CBD and more. Includes fixed-price tips from RPC Group.
body: If you're planning an office fitout in Melbourne, the first question is almost always 'How much will it cost?' The answer depends on several factors: the size of your space, the level of fitout, and your location. In Southbank and the CBD, commercial fitout costs generally range from $1,500 to $4,000 per square metre for a full design and build. But that's just a starting point — every project is different, and hidden costs can catch you out if you're not careful.

The biggest cost driver is the scope of work. A basic cosmetic refresh — new paint, carpet, and lighting — will be on the lower end. A full fitout with new partitions, mechanical systems, data cabling, and premium finishes pushes the price up. For example, a 200-square-metre office in Southbank might cost anywhere from $300,000 to $800,000 depending on whether you need structural changes or just a facelift. Always get a detailed fixed-price quote before committing.

Another key factor is the condition of the existing space. If you're taking over a new building, the base building infrastructure (air conditioning, power, fire systems) might already be in place, reducing costs. But if you're in an older building, you may need upgrades to meet current building codes. RPC Group always does a thorough site inspection to identify these issues early, so there are no surprises later.

Don't forget professional fees. Architects, engineers, and project managers typically add 10-15% to the total cost. However, using a design-and-build contractor like RPC Group can streamline this — we handle the design and project management in-house, often saving you money and time. We've seen clients save up to 20% by going with a single integrated team rather than separate consultants.

Location also matters. Fitout costs in premium precincts like Southbank or Collins Street can be higher due to access restrictions, building management requirements, and union agreements. If your office is in a heritage building, there are additional compliance costs. RPC Group has extensive experience navigating these local challenges, having completed dozens of fitouts in Melbourne's most iconic buildings.

Finally, timing affects cost. If you need a fast turnaround, you may need to pay overtime or expedite material orders. A standard fitout takes 6-12 weeks from design approval to handover. RPC Group uses a phased approach to keep the project moving without sacrificing quality. The key is to plan ahead and set a realistic budget — we'll help you prioritise what matters most to your business.

To get an accurate cost for your Melbourne office fitout, contact RPC Group for a free on-site consultation. We'll walk through your space, discuss your goals, and provide a transparent, fixed-price quote. No obligation, just honest advice from Southbank's trusted commercial builders.

Remember, a well-designed office is an investment in your team's productivity and your brand's image. With the right partner, you can achieve a stunning result without breaking the bank. Call us today on +61 3 9645 5210 or email admin@rparetail.com.

blogPosts.title: 5 Essential Tips for Office Make Good in Southbank
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning an end-of-lease make good in Southbank? Avoid costly penalties with these 5 tips from RPC Group. Includes timelines, landlord requirements and common pitfalls.
body: An office make good is often the last thing on a business owner's mind when moving out, but it can be one of the most expensive if done poorly. In Southbank and Melbourne's CBD, commercial leases usually require you to restore the space to its original condition. Failure to do so can result in losing your security deposit or facing legal claims. Here are five essential tips to make the process smooth and cost-effective.

1. Read Your Lease Early. The make good clause varies widely between landlords. Some require full demolition back to bare concrete, while others accept a 'clean and paint' standard. As soon as you know you're moving, dig out your lease and check the specifics. RPC Group can help interpret the jargon — we've handled make goods for dozens of Southbank offices and know what each landlord typically demands.

2. Start Planning at Least 3 Months Before Your Move. Make good works can take 4-8 weeks depending on the size of the space. You also need time for council permits if structural changes are involved. Starting late means rushed work or paying rent overlap. Our advice: budget for at least 2-3 months of planning and execution. RPC Group offers a free initial consultation to scope the work and provide a timeline.

3. Know Your Building's Rules. Many commercial buildings in Southbank have strict rules about after-hours work, waste disposal, and contractor permits. You may need to use the building's preferred contractors for fire services or asbestos removal. RPC Group is familiar with all the major Southbank building management teams and can coordinate approvals to avoid delays.

4. Get a Fixed-Price Quote for the Whole Job. Some contractors give a low initial quote and then add on charges for waste removal, protection, or cleaning. RPC Group provides a comprehensive fixed-price quote that covers everything — demolition, waste skip hire, painting, carpet removal, and restoration of services. No surprises, and no last-minute negotiations with the landlord.

5. Document Everything. Take photos of the space before you start and after completion. Keep copies of all approvals, waste disposal receipts, and sign-off from the building manager. This protects you if the landlord disputes the condition later. RPC Group includes a detailed handover report with every make good project, so you have peace of mind.

blogPosts.title: Restaurant Fitout Costs in Melbourne: A Complete 2026 Breakdown
blogPosts.excerpt: Opening a restaurant in Melbourne? Here's what you need to know about fitout costs, from kitchen equipment to dining area design. Local insights from RPC Group's Southbank team.
body: Melbourne's food scene is world-class, but opening a restaurant requires a significant upfront investment. Fitout costs can range from $200,000 for a small cafe to over $1.5 million for a full-service fine dining venue. The key is understanding where your money goes and how to maximise value. RPC Group has delivered restaurant fitouts across Melbourne, including Southbank, Docklands, and Fitzroy, and we've seen it all.

The largest single cost is the kitchen. Commercial kitchen fitouts typically account for 35-45% of the total budget. You need commercial-grade appliances, stainless steel benching, extraction systems, and fire suppression. In Melbourne, health department regulations require specific layout standards — easy-clean surfaces, adequate ventilation, and separate food handling zones. RPC Group works closely with commercial kitchen specialists to ensure compliance without overspending.

Dining area design is the next big ticket. Flooring, lighting, acoustic treatments, and furniture all add up. For a 100-seat restaurant, expect to spend $80,000 to $200,000 on fitout finishes. The trend in 2026 is sustainable materials and flexible layouts that can adapt to different service styles. We recommend spending more on lighting and acoustics — they dramatically affect the guest experience.

Don't forget the bar. A well-designed bar can become a profit centre itself. Bar fitouts include backlit displays, refrigerated units, shelving, and plumbing. Costs range from $30,000 for a simple setup to $150,000 for a fully custom bar with integrated technology. RPC Group's bar fitouts in Southbank have become talking points for their innovative use of space and lighting.

Permits and approvals are another major cost. You'll need building permits, health department approvals, liquor licensing, and possibly heritage approval if your venue is in a historic building. Allow 10-15% of your budget for these. RPC Group handles all the council and authority liaison as part of our project management service, saving you weeks of paperwork.

Timing matters too. If you're aiming for a summer opening, you may need to expedite the fitout, which can add 10-20% in labour premiums. The best approach is to start planning 6-9 months ahead. RPC Group uses a phased schedule that allows you to open sections of your venue sooner if needed.

Finally, always include a contingency of at least 10% for unforeseen issues — old wiring, asbestos, or structural surprises. In older Melbourne buildings, these are common. RPC Group's pre-fitout inspections identify these early, so you can plan your budget accurately.

For a detailed restaurant fitout quote in Melbourne, contact RPC Group. We'll visit your site, discuss your concept, and give you a transparent, fixed-price proposal. Let's bring your culinary vision to life in Southbank or wherever your venue calls home.

blogPosts.title: Retail Fitout Trends in Melbourne for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the latest retail fitout trends in Melbourne, from sustainable materials to interactive displays. RPC Group shares insights from recent Southbank and CBD projects.
body: Retail fitouts in Melbourne are evolving rapidly. Post-pandemic, shoppers expect more than just products — they want experiences. The best retail fitouts in 2026 blend digital technology with tactile design, creating spaces that engage all senses. RPC Group has been at the forefront of this shift, delivering innovative retail environments in Southbank, the CBD, and beyond.

Sustainability is no longer optional. More retailers are demanding eco-friendly materials — recycled timbers, low-VOC paints, and energy-efficient lighting. Brands that demonstrate environmental responsibility connect better with Melbourne's conscious consumers. RPC Group sources sustainable materials without compromising on aesthetics or durability, helping you meet your green goals.

Interactive technology is transforming store layouts. Digital screens, augmented reality fitting rooms, and contactless payment zones are becoming standard. However, these need to be integrated seamlessly into the fitout. RPC Group works with tech specialists to embed digital elements into the architecture, so they feel natural — not clunky add-ons.

Flexibility is key in 2026. Retail spaces need to adapt to different uses: a pop-up event one week, a private styling session the next. Modular fixtures, movable walls, and multi-purpose zones are in high demand. RPC Group designs retail fitouts with future-proofing in mind, so your space can evolve with your brand.

Lighting plays a crucial role. In Melbourne's often overcast climate, good artificial lighting can make or break a retail environment. We use layered lighting — ambient, task, and accent — to highlight products and guide customers through the store. LED strips, spotlights, and backlit displays create drama without high energy costs.

Local character matters too. Melbourne shoppers love stores that reflect the neighbourhood. A Southbank retail fitout might incorporate industrial elements like exposed brick and steel, while a Fitzroy store might lean into bohemian textures. RPC Group takes the time to understand your location and audience, ensuring your fitout feels authentic.

Budget is always a consideration. A full retail fitout in Melbourne typically costs between $1,500 and $3,500 per square metre, depending on complexity. RPC Group offers a free initial consultation to discuss your vision and provide a realistic budget range. We'll help you prioritise spending for maximum impact.

Whether you're launching a flagship store in the CBD or a boutique in Southbank, RPC Group has the expertise to deliver a retail fitout that stands out. Contact us today for a free quote and see how we can transform your retail space into a destination.
